title: Generation of Mature Toxoplasma gondii Bradyzoites in Human Immortalized Myogenic KD3 Cells
author: Deborah Maus
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare media and solutions
steps.instruction: Make all required culture media and reagents according to the listed compositions, keep sterile and store at 4 °C until use.

substeps.instruction: HFF growth medium: DMEM pH 7.2 (3.75 g/L NaHCO₃, 25 mM glucose, 4 mM L‑glutamine, 1 mM sodium pyruvate) + 1× penicillin/streptomycin + 10 % bovine serum.
Tachyzoite medium: same as HFF growth medium but with 1 % fetal bovine serum.
Myoblast growth medium: DMEM pH 7.2 (same salts) + 1× penicillin/streptomycin + 20 % fetal bovine serum + 2 % Ultroser® G.

Myoblast differentiation medium: DMEM pH 7.2 (same salts) + 1× penicillin/streptomycin + 2 % donor horse serum + 10 µg/mL human recombinant insulin (or Insulin Lispro) + 5 µg/mL human holo‑transferrin + 10 nM Na₂SeO₃.

Cyst medium: RPMI 1640 pH 7.4 (4 mM L‑glutamine) + 5 mM glucose + 1× penicillin/streptomycin + 50 mM HEPES + 2 % donor horse serum + 10 µg/mL insulin (or Lispro) + 5 µg/mL holo‑transferrin + 10 nM Na₂SeO₃.
Freezing medium: 90 % heat‑inactivated low‑endotoxin fetal bovine serum + 10 % DMSO.
Rat tail collagen I stock: 0.1 mg/mL collagen in 100 mM acetic acid; dilute 1:6.67 in water for coating.
1× Trypsin‑EDTA solution: 0.05 % trypsin / 0.53 mM EDTA in PBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺).
PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free): Milli‑Q water + 137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl, 1.5 mM KH₂PO₄, 6.5 mM Na₂HPO₄·2H₂O, pH 7.4.

steps.title: Thaw frozen KD3 myoblasts
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw cryovial, wash cells, and seed into a T‑75 flask with growth medium; incubate at 36.7 °C, 5–10 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: Warm myoblast growth medium to 37 °C in a water bath.
Sterilize work surface with 70 % ethanol.
Place cryovial on ice, then transfer to a 37 °C water bath until the outer layer melts.
Sterilize the cryovial with 70 % ethanol and transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube containing warm growth medium.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard supernatant, gently resuspend pellet in 15 mL warm growth medium.
Transfer suspension to a T‑75 flask (choose size for desired cell density) and incubate in a humidified incubator at 36.7 °C, 5–10 % CO₂.
Next day, inspect confluency and adhesion microscopically.

steps.title: Subculture KD3 myoblasts
steps.instruction: Passage cells before they reach 70 % confluence, using trypsin‑EDTA, and reseed at 6 × 10³ cells/cm².

substeps.instruction: Warm PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free) and 0.05 % trypsin/EDTA to room temperature; warm growth medium to 37 °C.
Sterilize work surface with 70 % ethanol.
Aspirate culture medium and wash monolayer with ≥10 mL pre‑warmed PBS.
Add 0.02 mL trypsin/EDTA per cm² of culture area; incubate at 36.7 °C (≈2 min) until cells detach.
Add enough warm growth medium to neutralize trypsin and pipette to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
Transfer suspension to a centrifuge tube and spin at 500 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in growth medium (0.3 mL per cm²).
Optional: Count cells with a hemocytometer and seed 6 × 10³ cells per cm² into new vessels.
Incubate at 36.7 °C, 5–10 % CO₂; 70 % confluence is typically reached in 2–3 days.

steps.title: Cryopreserve KD3 myoblasts (optional)
steps.instruction: Freeze low‑passage myoblasts before 70 % confluence using freezing medium and a controlled‑rate freezer.

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free) and trypsin/EDTA to room temperature; warm freezing medium to 37 °C.
Sterilize work surface with 70 % ethanol.
Aspirate medium, wash monolayer with ≥10 mL PBS.
Add 0.02 mL trypsin/EDTA per cm²; incubate at 37 °C (≈2 min) until detachment.
Add freezing medium to stop digestion, gently pipette to mix.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in growth medium.
Aliquot ~1.5–1.8 × 10⁶ cells (equivalent to 75 cm²) per cryovial.
Place cryovials in a controlled‑rate freezing container, freeze overnight at –70 °C, then transfer to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Differentiate KD3 myoblasts into myotubes
steps.instruction: Plate myoblasts, optionally coat with collagen, and induce fusion by switching to differentiation medium at 20–50 % confluence; culture for five days.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Coat culture vessels with 15 µg/mL rat tail collagen I for 1 h at room temperature, wash three times with PBS or let dry; store coated plastic at 4 °C if needed.
Plate 6 × 10³ cells per cm² in myoblast growth medium; incubate at 36.7 °C, 5–10 % CO₂.
Monitor confluence; when monolayer reaches 20–50 % (usually 1–2 days), begin differentiation.
Warm myoblast differentiation medium to 37 °C; sterilize surface with 70 % ethanol.
Aspirate growth medium, wash cells once with warm PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free) to remove residual serum.
Add differentiation medium and incubate at 36.7 °C, 5–10 % CO₂.
Maintain culture for five days; cells will fuse into multinucleated myotubes.
Optional: Verify fusion by immunofluorescence for myosin heavy chain and nuclei, calculate myogenic index.

steps.title: Infect myotubes and mature cysts
steps.instruction: Add tachyzoites to myotubes in cyst medium at 7.2 × 10³ parasites/cm², culture at 36.7 °C with ambient CO₂ for four weeks, changing medium every 2–3 days.

substeps.instruction: Maintain tachyzoites in HFF host cells per standard methods; obtain a freshly egressed or syringe‑released tachyzoite suspension.
Count parasites and prepare a dilution in cyst medium to achieve 7.2 × 10³ tachyzoites per cm² of myotube surface.
Wash myotube monolayer once with cyst medium, then add the parasite suspension.
Incubate at 36.7 °C in an incubator with ambient (≈0 %) CO₂.
Every second to third day, gently replace 75 % of the medium with fresh cyst medium, leaving 25 % to avoid disturbing the monolayer.
Monitor cultures daily by inverted microscopy for tachyzoite overgrowth, myotube detachment, or cyst loss; perform additional washes if overgrowth occurs.
After four weeks, cysts are considered functionally mature.

steps.title: Validate cyst maturation (optional)
steps.instruction: Assess bradyzoite markers and functional resistance to confirm cyst development.

substeps.instruction: Detect bradyzoite proteins BAG1, LDH2, p21 and loss of SAG1 by immunostaining or western blot.
Stain cyst walls with anti‑CST1, anti‑CC2 antibodies or Dolichos biflorus agglutinin (DBA).
Test functional maturation by exposing cysts (≥14 days) to 20 µM pyrimethamine and 20 µM sulfadiazine for one week and assess re‑differentiation.
Optionally, assess resistance to pepsin or temperature stress as additional functional read‑outs.
